output.brief:
Last week's 5xx rate (0.41%) is inside the normal range. Over the preceding 26 weeks the mean was 0.354% and the upper edge of the normal band was 0.482%. Three earlier weeks were higher, and investigating them found no fault. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). Customer impact is negligible: booking completion was flat (41.0% to 41.2%), retries succeeded 98.6% of the time, and there were no complaints. The dashboard count matches raw logs.

The "new pods error twice as often" finding is a cache warm-up effect. Every recent rollout shows it, including a redeploy of an unchanged image. It adds only 10–20 errors per rollout, so it doesn't explain roughly 2,000 extra errors in the week. It also doesn't show a fault in v4.18.

I did not test the replica move or partner-sync month-end traffic, so those stay open. Neither is needed to decide today.

Recommendation: don't roll back. Don't mute alerting; that would remove the only protection against a real problem. Note the week at ops review and run the standard check on the following week. If next week breaches the band, investigate then.
